item.title: 2026-10-20T21-07
item.description:
The Big List Of Naughty Strings is a cool project. It contains a list of ‘interesting’ strings that you can use in your testing - thinkings like SQL injection, RTL text, zero-width characters, emoji, Zalgo text and more. The project can be found here:

https://github.com/minimaxir/big-list-of-naughty-strings

I thought it might be interesting to wrap these up in a WireMock extension that adds a naughtyString Handlebars helper, so templated responses can return strings from the BLNS. That extension can be found here:

item.title: 2026-10-10T18-33
item.description:
Last week I put together a little Micronaut Framework WireMock extension to allow WireMock to be easily used inside tests. It uses the same annotations as the WireMock spring boot extension. At the moment it only supports http-based WireMock services but it does support the latest Micronaut and the latest WireMock OSS 4 beta so you get all the messaging and SSE support in there.

Along with that, I watched Faster Development with Java, Python, and Micronaut by Graeme Rocher and Thomas Wuerthinger from Devoxx Belgium. I have never been much of a python dev but Pyronaut looks amazing and definitely worth a try. Link to the video below.

item.title: 2026-09-27T16-52
item.description: Last week beta 39 of WireMock OSS v4 dropped. Along with the usual bug fixes and dependency updates, this release built on the messaging support already there to add support for Server Sent Events. This now opens up a wide range of testing capabilities and we are already making good use of this internally on the WireMock eng team. If you use SSE in your app I would love to hear what you think. I have updated the WireMock OSS docker example I have with a simple train departure board demo.

item.title: 2024-11-14T09:09
item.description: Even though LinkedIn jumped the gun a little, it is my 1 year anniversary at WireMock next week. The team has built some awesome dev tooling over the course of the last year - tooling that I wish I had access to in previous projects - OpenAPI, stateful mocking, mocks using your own data, gRPC and more. Not only that, it has been great to be a part of an active open source project with a great community behind it.
